name: Isombe
subtitle: Isombe is a traditional Rwandan stew of cassava leaves; in Rwanda the name is also used for cassava leaves preserved by drying.

facts.label: Name
facts.value: In Rwanda, isombe is the name of the (solar-)dried cassava leaf product; the Tanzanian equivalent is kisanvu

facts.label: Preservation
facts.value: In lowland areas of Rwanda where cassava is the main crop, cassava leaves are sun-dried until brittle and stored for eating through the long dry season

facts.label: Main ingredients
facts.value: Fresh vegetables combined with peanut butter; served as a side or main dish

facts.label: Who makes it
facts.value: Passed down in families: a Rwandan cook in Canada learned it from her grandmother

facts.label: Safety
facts.value: Cyanide remaining in boiled cassava leaves was judged safe because the vegetable is served in small quantities as a side food

facts.label: Safety advice
facts.value: Researchers advised against making cassava leaves an everyday food, especially for children, and recommended longer cooking

parts.text: Isombe is a traditional Rwandan stew of cassava leaves; in Rwanda the name is also used for cassava leaves preserved by drying. Cooked greens are combined with peanut butter, and palm oil may be added.

It can be served as a side or a main dish, with rice and bread. Researchers studying cassava-leaf preparations in Rwanda note the vegetable is eaten in small quantities as a side food and advise against making it an everyday food for children.
